page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Multiply and divide by sin x
steps.margin_note: First mark. The standard limit is (eᵗ − 1)/t, so the denominator must be made to match the power. Here the power is sin x, so sin x is the quantity that must appear underneath.
steps.memory_tip: Whatever sits in the power of e must also sit in the denominator. Supply it, and pay for it with a second fraction.
lines: Putting x = 0 gives 0/0, so the expression is rewritten first.
For x close to 0 with x ≠ 0 we have sin x ≠ 0, so we may multiply and divide by sin x.
∴ lim(x → 0) (e^(sin x) − 1)/x = lim(x → 0) (e^(sin x) − 1)/sin x · lim(x → 0) (sin x)/x

recall.must_convey: That the expression is multiplied and divided by sin x, which is allowed because sin x ≠ 0 near 0 apart from at 0 itself.
accept: multiply and divide by sin x
put sin x underneath so it matches the power of e
sin x is not zero near zero except at zero, so dividing is allowed
sin x tho multiply chesi divide cheyyali
break it into e power sin x minus one over sin x times sin x over x

steps.why: The standard limit is (eᵗ − 1)/t → 1, so the denominator has to carry the same quantity as the power. A limit at 0 only looks at values with x ≠ 0, and for those x near 0 the value sin x is not zero, so dividing by sin x is legal there. This is the reason the multiply-and-divide is allowed and not a division by zero.
common_mistakes: Multiplying and dividing by x instead of sin x, which leaves the power and the denominator unmatched.
Writing (e^(sin x) − 1)/x = (eˣ − 1)/x by dropping the sine from the power.

steps.label: Apply the two standard limits
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Say that sin x → 0 as x → 0, so the first factor is the standard limit with t = sin x. Both factors are 1, so the product is 1.
steps.memory_tip: Both factors are worth 1, so the answer is 1 × 1.
lines: As x → 0, sin x → 0. Put t = sin x, then t → 0.

recall.must_convey: That with t = sin x the first factor is 1 and sin x/x is 1, so the answer is 1.
accept: put t equals sin x so it becomes e power t minus one over t which is one
both factors are one so the answer is one
sin x tends to zero so the first part is the standard limit
sin x ni t ga teesukunte answer one vasthundi

steps.why: The substitution t = sin x is what turns the first factor into the standard limit. Stating that t → 0 as x → 0 is the part that makes the substitution valid, and it is what the examiner looks for.
common_mistakes: Writing the first factor as 1 without saying that sin x → 0.
Multiplying the two factors and giving 2 instead of 1.
